audit.release_evidence: GitHub reports exact candidate tests, publication, public provenance verification and post-deploy live smoke successful. Candidate archive and payload digests independently recomputed in the audit container.
audit.local_runtime: Node 22.16.0 for isolated compiled probes; not the repository supported source-test environment
audit.scope: Fresh original-source inspection of implicated implementations and counterpart tests, exact deployed-candidate analysis, 11 isolated current-artifact probes, all 37 prior findings and 43 prior task records dispositioned.
limitations: Browser navigation to live and localhost was blocked by administrator policy. No firsthand live gameplay, browser layout, audio audition or physical-device claim is made.
No full local Git checkout, supported-Node-24 source build, complete original test-suite rerun or local PostgreSQL/Deno execution was completed. Source was read through the connected GitHub tools.
Some files were read completely; some as complete implicated methods. The ledger records this. This is not a claim to have read every file in the repository.

The full new reward SQL/worker implementation and hosted database/function/configuration state were not comprehensively independently attested. Inspecting completion and client contracts is not a security certification of the whole reward subsystem.
Reproduction scripts use exact current compiled code with disclosed fixtures. They demonstrate pinned behavior, not an implemented fix, nor replacement acceptance tests for future code.
No measured player-retention or acquisition dataset was available; product proposals are hypotheses and study designs.

product_contract.resourcing: Solo implementation; no outside staff or paid service assumed
product_contract.decision_rule: Ship justified corrections and observe play; do not make cleanup or verified-reward infrastructure a prerequisite for every ordinary content experiment.

orchestration.model_assignment_notice: Logical requested model names. Resolve real selectable IDs and supported efforts in T00; these assignments are planning heuristics, not measured comparative benchmarks.
orchestration.collision_rule: Tasks with intersecting scope paths or exclusive_locks must not write concurrently. Serialize the NetworkClient lane. Main/HUD/input work shares one integrator. Independent worktrees; parent merges after evidence review.
worker_rules: Read complete current implicated definitions and relevant tests before editing.
One bounded behavior change per task; no blanket migration, package replacement or formatting sweep.
Write an original-source failing regression, implement, and prove the new postcondition.
Never weaken security controls, branch checks, test prerequisites or compatibility rules to satisfy a plan.
Use current repository commands and supported runtimes. Audit reproductions remain historical evidence.
No production writes, release dispatch, database changes, public issue creation or external service purchase without separate authorization.
Human studies and visual/audio judgments require actual human/runtime evidence.
Record actual model/effort, source head, changed paths, tests, residual risk and review result for every task.

recovery_gate.policy: Finite correction gate. Qualification risks T08/T09 must be explicitly dispositioned before release; a nonreproduced risk may close with evidence, not with a forced refactor. Blocked qualification requires recorded residual risk and explicit owner acceptance; it cannot be labeled passed. Product evidence can start once the relevant user-facing fixes are integrated; it does not wait for T13.
non_goals: Rewrite of applied migrations or retained CQ1 editions

findings.title: A successful rematch can still fail to take the player into its successor
findings.evidence: requestRematch returns success but discards the response roomId. Migration is driven by a rooms UPDATE notification. The server returns an existing successor without creating another UPDATE. In P01, two successful retry responses produced zero handoffs when no Realtime notification was delivered.
findings.why_it_matters: A player can press the correct recovery control, receive success, and stay on the finished game. Retrying does not necessarily repair a missed notification. The server-side allocation can be correct while the player journey is broken.
findings.solo_remedy: Pass the returned successor ID into one generation-safe handoff function shared with Realtime. Fetch the authoritative successor row through the existing reader before constructing the new client. Do not construct from the abbreviated restart response: its room/player projection does not contain the full configuration used by handleRematch. Keep one callback, one client generation and one saved descriptor.
findings.mature_team_approach: Separate durable command acknowledgment from best-effort notification delivery. A durable acknowledgment supplies an identity that a convergent state reader can resolve. Exercise response/event reorderings, duplicates and lost notifications as transport faults.
findings.verification: Original-source regression: suppress UPDATE, return a real successor identifier, and assert exactly one handoff. Deliver UPDATE before and after HTTP completion, retry an existing successor, then leave during lookup. Compare the complete authoritative roster, teams, AI metadata, rounds, economy, hazard and ruleset settings.
findings.keep: Existing restart RPC, private seat token, authoritative room fetch, rematchToConfig and MatchSessionLifecycle.
findings.limitations: Isolated client reproduction; no production rematch or server mutation was performed. A normal delivered Realtime event can complete the existing path.

findings.title: History recovery consumes one response page, not a complete ordered history
findings.evidence: initialize/resyncLog do not page the room-action query. The repository API configuration caps a response at 1000 rows. P03 used the same capped-query behavior with a three-row fixture limit: a seven-row log yielded one query, three applied rows, and four unread rows.
findings.why_it_matters: Long matches or recovery after a prolonged interruption can leave a client behind while a read operation itself succeeds. The new revision protocol prevents several bad writes, but it does not make a partial history complete. Raising the server row limit merely moves the threshold.
findings.solo_remedy: Read ordered pages to a captured target revision, using the existing OrderedActionSession. Prefer a sequence cursor over shifting offsets. Bound total work, yield during replay, detect missing sequences, and expose recovering versus caught-up. Do not enable command submission until canonical recovery reaches its target. Retain rows arriving via Realtime during catch-up.
findings.mature_team_approach: Use a resumable log reader with explicit watermarks, backpressure, bounded snapshots or checkpoints when warranted, and liveness metrics. The read protocol should prove completion, not infer it from a successful first response.
findings.verification: Test histories of 0, pageSize-1, pageSize, pageSize+1 and several pages; missing/duplicate rows; concurrent appends; read failure on page two; cancellation after page one. Compare all state and terrain with complete ordered replay. Never mark a gap recovered.
findings.keep: OrderedActionSession, sequence ordering and the revision-checked command transaction. No new realtime backend or mandatory snapshot format.
findings.limitations: The hosted API cap was not independently queried. The source contains max_rows=1000; the probe deliberately used three as a scaled fixture. No real long production room was observed.

findings.title: CPU settlement states lose the distinction between refusal, conflict and transient failure
findings.evidence: On a permanent 403 invalid_seat_token, the real network submission path clears its attempt and is eligible again on the next logical callback. P04 observed five submissions over five callbacks. On a revision conflict with failed catch-up and no incoming row, P05 retained settlement=conflict across 61 callbacks with no local command watchdog.
findings.why_it_matters: One branch can repeatedly send work that cannot succeed; the other can wait indefinitely while transport appears connected. These are recovery-state bugs, not a recurrence of the old expensive planner or missing accessory implementation.
findings.solo_remedy: Introduce explicit settlement outcomes in the existing command driver: accepted-awaiting-row, retryable-transport, revision-conflict-recovering, terminal-authorization/protocol refusal, and disposed. Terminal refusal stops automatic submission and offers a clear recovery action. Conflict drives bounded canonical recovery and re-evaluates only after observed progress. Reuse a logical intent through ambiguity rather than minting replacements blindly.
findings.mature_team_approach: Treat command delivery as a finite state machine with a monotonic generation/revision basis, bounded retries, acknowledgments and observable terminal failure. Test event sequences, not only isolated HTTP status mapping.
findings.verification: 403/invalid seat and unsupported protocol cause no repeated posts. 429 and transport faults respect bounded delay. A conflict followed by a lost row and failed first read recovers or becomes actionable without relying on a socket reconnect. Accepted-but-unseen commands retain identity. Teardown cancels all retries.
findings.keep: Correct getBotPlan cache, weapon/accessory preparation sequence, deterministic CPU intent identity and atomic SQL fencing.
findings.limitations: Planner and next-seat computation were injected fixed ports in P04/P05. Their call counts are not a measurement of real planning cost. A later reconnect can recover the existing conflict path; the gap is autonomous recovery while the link remains connected.

findings.title: A finite poll count does not bound a read that never settles
findings.evidence: handleRematch has a 20-attempt polling limit but the individual successor read has no deadline. Initialization and rematch request/recovery also contain unbounded waits outside the existing command/resync deadline helpers. P02 stopped at the first never-settling query, not the twentieth attempt.
findings.why_it_matters: A stalled dependency can hold the match transition indefinitely. Counting attempts limits completed failures, not a hanging Promise. This undermines the visible retry path precisely when users need it.
findings.solo_remedy: Apply the existing deadline/cancellation pattern to admission and successor reads, with one overall transition budget and smaller per-read limits. Propagate cancellation/generation checks into completion. Show retry/return controls when the bounded budget expires. Preserve the same successor identity on retry.
findings.mature_team_approach: Make async resource acquisition have an explicit deadline, cancellation owner and terminal outcome. Fault-inject black-holed reads separately from rejected reads; observe both latency and leak behavior.
findings.verification: A never-settling query, a response arriving after timeout, repeated retry, and leave-during-lookup must all produce a bounded outcome without creating stale clients or duplicate handoffs. Use fake timers for tests rather than waiting out production timeouts.
findings.keep: Existing settleWithDeadline and abort semantics; do not add another retry library or replace the transport.
findings.limitations: The 30ms probe window is only evidence that the first await remained pending. It is not a recommended user timeout or a measured production outage.

findings.title: The verified challenge rejects commands that the shared controls still advertise
findings.evidence: VerifiedChallengeClient accepts only set_angle, set_power and fire. The shared HUD projection still exposes ordinary movement, weapon cycling and armory actions. InputHandler advances its own weapon cursor even when a challenge selection is ignored. P09 cycled to Shield: Fire emitted use_shield, the retained controller stayed on Baby Missile in PLAYER_TURN, and no fire was recorded.
findings.why_it_matters: The page can appear responsive while doing nothing, and an unrelated weapon action can make the primary fire command stop working. Correct authority enforcement is present; the missing piece is an honest input/presentation capability boundary.
findings.solo_remedy: Project a small typed set of mode capabilities into HUD and InputHandler: legal aim/power bounds, committed attack kind, movement, cycling and buying. Hide or clearly disable inapplicable controls with a mode-specific explanation. Derive the primary attack from authoritative mode/tank state, not an independently advanced unsupported cursor. Keep the controller as the final enforcement boundary.
findings.mature_team_approach: Model capabilities explicitly at the UI/application boundary and test view/intent/domain parity for every mode. Reuse the same semantic controls where they are legal; do not force every mode to support the whole ordinary-game command vocabulary.
findings.verification: In CQ1, pointer and keyboard aim and fire still work after every visible/keyboard command. Q, movement and buy/equip cannot advance hidden local input state. Ordinary hot-seat and online modes retain stock, movement and shields. Test denied commands, menu return, resume and fixed power=100 challenge limits.
findings.keep: Retained CQ1 controller and reward verification, GameSessionComposition, shared semantic controls, and strict replay contract. No generalized plugin/mode framework is needed.
findings.limitations: Real challenge controller/client and InputHandler were executed together; current main/HUD forwarding was read separately. No complete browser-page journey was navigated here. This is not a server authorization bypass.

findings.title: Armory confuses a purchase tier with permission to equip owned ammunition
findings.evidence: battleConsoleArmoryItems requires arms-level unlock for canEquip as well as canBuy. A real arms-level-0 engine starts with one Heavy Missile, whose purchase tier is 1. P07 found canEquip=false in the actual HUD method while the same engine accepted selection and firing. Keyboard cycling can reach the item independently.
findings.why_it_matters: The new Lean Arsenal promise is to preserve an opening kit while restricting restocks. The UI withholds part of that kit and disagrees with another input path. This changes perceived tactical variety and can make a challenge appear unfair or confusing.
findings.solo_remedy: Keep the arms-level condition for buying. Allow equipping an owned, implemented and currently permitted weapon regardless of its purchase tier. Apply mode capability restrictions separately. Explain locked restocks without labeling existing stock unusable.
findings.mature_team_approach: Separate acquisition eligibility, possession, equip eligibility and use eligibility as different policies. Reuse policy projections across input paths so catalog labels cannot redefine engine rules.
findings.verification: At arms levels 0–4, verify owned above-tier ammo is equippable, unowned stock is not, purchases stay tier-limited, and shields route correctly. Compare Armory, Q and direct command behavior in ordinary modes. CQ1 still rejects non-Baby weapons through its mode capabilities.
findings.keep: Existing economy and inventory; no weapon rebalance, starting-loadout change or new content system.
findings.limitations: Actual compiled HUD projection and engine were executed without a browser DOM. Full original applyAction/applyBuy and HUD projection methods were read.

findings.title: A drag below the tank on its left flips aim to the right
findings.evidence: applyPointerAim clamps every negative atan2 result to zero. Below-left and below-right vectors are both negative, so both become rightward zero degrees. P08 used a pivot at (600,250) and pointer at (500,300): the emitted angle was 0.
findings.why_it_matters: Touch and mouse aiming should remain directionally understandable at a boundary. An unintended 180-degree reversal is a feel/correctness defect, particularly during an imprecise finger drag.
findings.solo_remedy: Define the allowed upper-hemisphere projection explicitly. Clamp below-left to the left horizontal boundary and below-right to the right boundary, with a documented tie at the pivot. Preserve existing coordinate normalization, power cap, pointer capture and input gates.
findings.mature_team_approach: Express coordinate conversions as small tested geometry functions, including quadrant boundaries, mirrored positions, CSS scaling and degenerate rectangles. Keep direction semantics independent of input device.
findings.verification: Test all four quadrants, exactly horizontal/vertical, pivot, CSS-scaled canvas, zero-size rectangle and high-cap tanks. Confirm the barrel visually follows the emitted direction on a real touch device before changing sensitivity.
findings.keep: The actual InputHandler and its recently repaired focus return. No engine or gesture library replacement.
findings.limitations: The actual pointer math was executed with an injected DOM rectangle. This was not physical-device interaction or a complete drag event sequence.

findings.title: Persisted-page restoration has no matching lifecycle path
findings.evidence: main installs a once-only pagehide handler that permanently destroys HUD. HUD latches destroyed=true and subsequent update calls return early. The complete entrypoint contains no pageshow restoration, and a repository search returned no pageshow matches.
findings.why_it_matters: A page retained in the back/forward cache can return without a new bootstrap. The retained application may still hold a permanently destroyed presentation owner. Mobile and history navigation need explicit restore behavior, not the assumption that pagehide always means final disposal.
findings.solo_remedy: First reproduce with real history navigation and inspect event.persisted. Separate suspend/restore from final teardown using the current lifecycle owners. On restore, refresh clock baselines, credentials/session eligibility and subscriptions without double-binding. Do not bypass BFCache or automatically forfeit a network seat on transient page hiding.
findings.mature_team_approach: Maintain a documented page lifecycle state machine and browser-engine matrix, with suspension, resume and final disposal tested independently. Retained server receipts and expiring sessions remain authoritative after restoration.
findings.verification: Navigate away and back with persisted=true in supported browser engines; test hot-seat, online and CQ1, expired credentials, expired challenge, audio resume and repeated cycles. A rejected hypothesis closes with traces and no speculative rewrite.
findings.keep: Current generation-based session ownership and per-mode expiry rules.
findings.limitations: Source-derived risk, not a reproduced BFCache failure here. Browser navigation was blocked. MDN documents the relevant event semantics; runtime qualification precedes remediation.

findings.title: CQ1 opens its report before the ordinary impact-completion handoff
findings.evidence: The main state listener synchronizes challenge result presentation before rendering the corresponding state. setVerifiedChallenge immediately updates its dedicated view. That view opens on a local result or completion-pending status, unlike the ordinary terminal path that waits for renderer impact completion.
findings.why_it_matters: A correct one-shot clear can be covered by a verification report before the player reads the hit. The new outcome copy emphasizes local/server receipt distinctions; those distinctions should not consume the payoff of the tactical action.
findings.solo_remedy: Capture an actual early-clear sequence first. Keep server completion independent, but delay only the dominant report presentation until the existing impact signal (or a bounded fallback) says the result is readable. Show a small nonblocking verification state meanwhile. Restore completed attempts without replaying historical explosions.
findings.mature_team_approach: Keep domain completion, reward settlement and presentation choreography as separate state transitions. Define timeline acceptance for both natural termination and nonlethal objective completion, including reduced motion and reload.
findings.verification: Record frames from the first damaging shot through local outcome and receipt. Assert no blocking report before the last meaningful impact cue, no unbounded wait, no duplicate reward request, and immediate silent presentation when restoring an already completed receipt.
findings.keep: Dedicated truthful challenge receipt view and the existing ordinary impact-completion mechanism. Do not change retained verifier semantics for cosmetic timing.
findings.limitations: Ordering is confirmed in source; actual perceptual occlusion and appropriate timing were not observed in a browser. Treat as a bounded visual investigation, not a claimed measured feel regression.

findings.title: Desktop control behavior still depends on captured English labels
findings.evidence: SemanticContractTree still interprets accessible-name text to choose actions and render dynamic states. The payload reduction removed archival bulk, but did not remove this coupling. A wording/localization change can remain a behavior change.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a demonstrated reason for a narrow refactor: it couples player copy, accessibility names and command identity. File length is not the reason. The current compact explicit-control pattern provides a reference for the replacement.
findings.solo_remedy: Replace the wide/standard snapshot interpreter with explicit typed semantic controls using the current presentation state and intent adapter. Preserve layout, focus identities, disabled behavior and the separate Pixi decoration. Retire the interpreter only after behavior parity and deliberate label-change tests pass.
findings.mature_team_approach: Use typed action identifiers and presentation projections, keeping accessibility names descriptive rather than executable. Maintain an independent control/intent contract and visual regression coverage across breakpoints.
findings.verification: Change a visible/accessible label without changing its action; mutate an action ID and require tests to fail. Exercise keyboard, pointer, disabled states, focus across breakpoints, inventory and CQ1 restrictions. Compare artifact size and preserve semantic-first readiness.
findings.keep: Preact, current intent adapter, compact controls, current CSS/Pixi appearance, and existing resource ledger.
findings.limitations: Source coupling is confirmed. No production localization defect was observed. This refactor is not a prerequisite for shipping the smaller correctness fixes.

findings.title: The repaired terminal-collapse proof still has sibling skip-to-green paths
findings.evidence: Path B now fails missing prerequisites and observes real pending flushes. Paths A and D still log SKIPPED when their required scenario is not reached, without setting failed. The final summary exits zero if nothing else failed.
findings.why_it_matters: The original terminal regression is genuinely repaired, but a future change can make either sibling fixture stop exercising its claimed contract while the harness remains green. This is a remaining proof obligation, not evidence that current physics is wrong.
findings.solo_remedy: Make required A/D fixture prerequisites fail with targeted diagnostics. If a subcase is genuinely unreachable, label it out of scope instead of counting it as passed. Add negative controls showing each exercised behavior and missing-fixture condition fails independently.
findings.mature_team_approach: Distinguish required regression tests from exploratory searches. Required tests must prove setup and outcome; exploratory coverage should report a denominator and uncovered scenarios without masquerading as a gate.
findings.verification: Run the normal fixture and three negative cases for each path: no scenario reached, intended behavior disabled, and unrelated behavior changed. Preserve repaired Path B controls and do not broaden assertions beyond the reachable weapon set.
findings.keep: Current real physics harness and the new Path B instrumentation. No replacement test framework is needed.
findings.limitations: Original A/B/D/summary source was read. These new negative controls were not run against the original source suite in this environment.

findings.title: The largest measured distribution cost is now artwork, not the removed contract archive
findings.evidence: The exact candidate contains 26 image files totaling 9,599,438 bytes of 11,933,441 payload bytes. The console chunk is now 235,015 bytes versus the old 4,208,428. The optional decoration adapter still requests all responsive texture modes through one process-owned cache, and the semantic root preloads the three semantic atlases plus match and armory frames.
findings.why_it_matters: The main payload problem changed. Further splitting of the already-shrunk console cannot substitute for knowing which images load before first input, how large they decode, and whether repeated matches retain them. But total artifact bytes are not the same as first-session transfer.
findings.solo_remedy: Measure cold/warm first-input timing, request waterfalls and decoded allocations on the actual target devices. Then trial one highest-cost asset change, such as right-sizing the splash/settings frame or fetching the active chrome mode first. Preserve fast semantic readiness and compare actual readability, not only file size.
findings.mature_team_approach: Use scene-level asset budgets, staged loading, stable cache identities, texture lifetimes and device-specific profiling. Consider GPU changes only after a profile shows the Canvas world is the bottleneck.
findings.verification: Before/after fixed-device traces with identical network conditions, first useful controls, first shot, mode switch and ten match cycles. Record bytes requested rather than summing all disk assets. Verify fallback art and no layout regression. No optimization is accepted on invented FPS estimates.
findings.keep: Three authored world backgrounds, modular tank art, semantic-first HUD and the current browser distribution. No mandatory engine/native migration.
findings.limitations: Disk/raw/gzip sizes and image dimensions are measured. Network transfer, decode timing, GPU memory and on-device frame performance were not measured. The contact sheet shows source assets, not gameplay screenshots.

findings.title: The product now has a learning loop; its replay value still needs human evidence
findings.evidence: The current registry has six operations including First Salvo and explicit practice objectives; the chooser gives First Salvo a privileged first-session path. ST1 seed sharing exists. CQ1 is a retained, three-human-salvo, fixed-seed qualification with a one-time medal/200-XP reward. No new behavioral player data was provided for this review.
findings.why_it_matters: It would be wrong to prescribe these features as missing. The next uncertainty is whether players understand a useful decision, notice the result, and choose another tactical problem. More receipt infrastructure, more cards or public matchmaking do not answer that by themselves.
findings.solo_remedy: Observe a small willing sample using the unmodified first-entry flow. Ask them to choose and explain their next action without coaching. Compare first meaningful hit, voluntary replay and ability to explain an objective. Use the existing manual observation/report templates, then change one observed friction point or author one distinct next challenge.
findings.mature_team_approach: Separate acquisition, activation, within-session replay and return behavior. Combine qualitative observation with minimal consent-aware events when needed; choose a content hypothesis before building a generalized progression or analytics system.
findings.verification: Report participant counts and exact observations, not a fabricated retention percentage or an industry benchmark. Keep visitors who abandon in the denominator. Confirm any proposed next challenge creates a different tactical choice rather than a reskin or compulsory grind.
findings.keep: Free guest browser entry, First Salvo, Quick Operations, Field Orders, honest verified rewards and credential-free seed sharing.
findings.limitations: This is a product recommendation, not a causal diagnosis of why friends stopped playing. Authenticated CQ1 and physical-device experience were not personally played in this pass.

previous_findings.previous_title: A build can be published before the full CI result exists
previous_findings.assessment: Exact-source CI, transported candidate tests, publication revalidation and current successful Pages evidence replace the former build-only promotion. Browser checks are now required. Do not rebuild this pipeline again.

previous_findings.previous_title: Unique sequence allocation is not command idempotency or atomic authorization
previous_findings.assessment: Migration 021 moves credential, revision and intent decisions into the locked transaction. Client intent identity exists. Remaining delivery/recovery failures are N01–N04, not the original allocation race.

previous_findings.previous_title: Casual-room clients still decide facts the referee uses to admit commands
previous_findings.assessment: Casual command admission is still not authoritative physics or proof of human play. Keep the casual/verified distinction; no ranked or valuable prize claim follows from lockstep.

previous_findings.previous_title: Room completion and scoreboard publication can disagree
previous_findings.assessment: Migration 022 unifies room completion, score normalization and immutable result receipt. The previous split-write plan is obsolete. Hosted definitions still need operational attestation.

previous_findings.previous_title: The appearance probe can prove its own marker instead of the real control
previous_findings.assessment: Current mount no longer imports or publishes the appearance-probe/retirement machinery. Preserve actual browser controls/tests rather than replacing every existing test. This is not a certification of every historical test.

previous_findings.previous_title: Governance contracts are part of a 4.21 MB production JavaScript chunk
previous_findings.assessment: The exact current console chunk is 235,015 bytes, down from 4,208,428. Runtime archive import protection exists. Remaining English-name interpretation is a different issue.

previous_findings.previous_title: Decorative chrome readiness is coupled to loading every responsive asset mode
previous_findings.assessment: Semantic controls no longer wait for every decorative texture. Optional all-mode texture loading remains behind a bounded cached adapter; optimize only from device/waterfall measurements.

previous_findings.previous_title: Production code spoofs Pixi hardware probes to satisfy lifecycle constraints
previous_findings.assessment: The complete current Pixi adapter no longer spoofs capability probes. It uses bounded shared admission, standard initialization and removable waiters.

previous_findings.previous_title: Deterministic ticks are paced by display refresh rate
previous_findings.assessment: Current FrameClock yields 60 logical beats at 30/60/120/144Hz in P06; both clients use clock/generation guards. End-to-end visual/audio pacing still requires device traces.

previous_findings.previous_title: A required collapse scenario can skip and leave the harness green
previous_findings.assessment: The original Path B gap is repaired with setup and flush observations. Sibling A/D skip-to-green conditions remain; do not reimplement Path B.

previous_findings.previous_title: The migration guard can silently lose its history comparison
previous_findings.assessment: Explicit resolvable base/head refs, base-tree migration inventory and fatal Git errors replace silent HEAD^ fallback.

previous_findings.previous_title: Specialist tests already run; target the remaining browser/normal-entry gaps
previous_findings.assessment: Exact transported candidate browser suites and required browser protection are real improvements. Current default projects remain Chromium-based; physical-device and unsupported-engine claims require separate proof.

previous_findings.previous_title: The engine exposes mutable internal state as a snapshot
previous_findings.assessment: The earlier main-owned verified-terminal mutation was replaced by a presentation projection. GameEngine still returns a mutable borrowed state. Do not deep-copy terrain per frame or impose a repository-wide readonly rewrite without a new demonstrated write.

previous_findings.previous_title: No generic engine or coordinator extraction is justified by this pass
previous_findings.assessment: A mandatory whole-engine/coordinator extraction remains unjustified. Existing methods and resource owners should remain unless a concrete change demonstrates a missing boundary.

previous_findings.previous_title: Historical guidance contradicts the implementation and can misdirect agents
previous_findings.assessment: Do not treat old review plans as active law. Even current applyBuy comments still say bots do not buy accessories, while the planner/driver do. Fix contradictory current guidance alongside the affected implementation; do not undertake an archive purification project.

previous_findings.previous_title: Backend deployment is manual, but not yet a reproducible release transaction
previous_findings.assessment: Backend workflow now binds main, manifest, CLI and CI, uses a protected environment, dry-run/readback and a receipt. The actual environment/hosted functions were not independently attested. Do not replace it on the old premise.

previous_findings.previous_title: Art already exists; distribution and decoded-memory budgets need equal attention
previous_findings.assessment: Authored assets exist and dominate measured disk bytes. Profile actual loading and allocation before selecting optimizations.

previous_findings.previous_title: Replay chunking bounds actions, not the work inside one action
previous_findings.assessment: Bounded verification work is now present in the engine/challenge completion path. Casual replay still needs complete paged history and bounded work; address that reader first, not an unconditional worker/WASM rewrite.

previous_findings.previous_title: Replay verification proves an allowed result, not a human or varied challenge
previous_findings.assessment: CQ1 now supplies an explicit fixed qualification and reward contract. It is not a proof of human play or an unlimited variety loop. Preserve the artifact, then test replay value.

previous_findings.previous_title: Keep dirty rendering; fix demonstrated repeated network CPU planning
previous_findings.assessment: Keep dirty rendering. The network planner cache and preparation handling exist. New settlement retry defects must not be confused with the earlier every-frame planning defect.

previous_findings.previous_title: A synth-only rule is an implementation constraint, not a product requirement
previous_findings.assessment: No new listening session was possible. A hybrid-audio audition remains a conditional product experiment, not a confirmed current audio defect or a required dependency migration.

previous_findings.previous_title: Modal behavior is being hand-implemented in multiple UI owners
previous_findings.assessment: Retain independent dialog policy. The new CQ1 view has its own retry and return behavior. There is no mandate to consolidate all modals merely because mechanisms resemble each other.

previous_findings.previous_title: Landscape-only mobile support is a product and accessibility decision
previous_findings.assessment: The current test setup still describes landscape phone play. Real orientation, restore, touch and safe-area testing precede a native decision.

previous_findings.previous_title: There is no evidence yet for a retention diagnosis
previous_findings.assessment: No new player observations or retention dataset was supplied. The inspected product-evidence directory exposed templates, not an observed cohort. This does not assert that no private evidence exists elsewhere.

previous_findings.previous_title: Reuse existing Field Orders instead of inventing another objective subsystem
previous_findings.assessment: Explicit practice objectives now use the existing operation path. Do not invent another objective framework; validate current tasks before expanding.

previous_findings.previous_title: The quick path still asks for choices before the player understands them
previous_findings.assessment: First Salvo now has a privileged first-session path and other choices can be secondary. Reassess actual first-use comprehension rather than repeating the old missing-onboarding prescription.

previous_findings.previous_title: An after-action report is present; a strong next reason to play is still a hypothesis
previous_findings.assessment: Practice identity and public seed sharing improve the post-match proposition. CQ1 report choreography and human next-choice behavior still warrant observation.

previous_findings.previous_title: No simultaneous audience should be required for the first good session
previous_findings.assessment: Bots, curated solo practice and credential-free asynchronous seed challenges reduce the need for a simultaneous population. Public matchmaking is not the next required build.

previous_findings.previous_title: Balance and feel need a measurement loop separate from correctness tests
previous_findings.assessment: Correctness and fixed-seed replay are not balance or fun measurements. Use a scenario/observation notebook; do not rebalance retained challenge editions in place.

previous_findings.previous_title: The asset direction is stronger than a wholesale visual restart would imply
previous_findings.assessment: The actual three-world backgrounds, modular tank sheet and chrome were inspected as source assets. A coherent direction exists; improve gameplay-scale hierarchy instead of restarting the skin.

previous_findings.previous_title: Hard CPU can choose an arms-level-forbidden restock and fail to advance
previous_findings.assessment: The current CPU planner respects arms-level purchase eligibility. P11 reproduced a legal Baby Missile fallback with exhausted finite ammo and 15,000 credits at arms level 0.

previous_findings.previous_title: Ordinary CPU target selection can aim at its own team
previous_findings.assessment: nearestEnemy now excludes same-team targets when team metadata is present. Preserve free-for-all behavior; do not repeat the earlier fix task.

previous_findings.previous_title: Network CPU execution repeats planning and drops accessory intents
previous_findings.assessment: Current network execution caches the plan and handles weapon/accessory preparation. Remaining refusal/conflict settlement needs N03, not another cache rewrite.

previous_findings.previous_title: Aim guide applies sudden-death gravity using global rather than round-local turns
previous_findings.assessment: main now supplies the client effective-gravity read instead of recomputing sudden death from global turns.

previous_findings.previous_title: Battery upgrades are accepted by the engine but unreachable through human power controls
previous_findings.assessment: Power cap is supplied to InputHandler and HUD. P10 bought a Battery, observed cap=200, and reached power=150 through the actual input method.

previous_findings.previous_title: Wide controls interpret historical accessible-name text as action identifiers
previous_findings.assessment: Desktop snapshot interpretation still dispatches by English label. This supports the narrow typed-control refactor, not a whole-HUD rewrite.

previous_findings.previous_title: Hot-seat stop can be undone by the running emission callback
previous_findings.assessment: Current local/network loops use running/generation checks after callbacks before rearming. Preserve these guards in all new mode work.
